**2026-10-29.** A patch release about durable throughput, plus two small fixes. Everything in the
v0.6.0 release notes applies. The snapshot format and the database schema are unchanged,
so an instance parked by a 0.6.4 engine resumes under 0.6.5, and there is no migration. The `q:`
namespace is untouched.

## Why

A relay of two processes — an HTTP intake that is validated, a forward over a local channel to a
second process, its answer relayed back, then an HTTP callback — completed about 14 relays per
second on a 12-core laptop, whatever the offered rate. The engine was idle (a tenth of a core); the
time went into waiting for the disk. Each relay cost 12 WAL flushes, every one its own
transaction, issued one after another by a single outbox loop, so no two ever shared a flush. A
consumer NVMe flushes about 325 times a second.

Only three of those twelve commits carry state that must be on disk before anything is
acknowledged: the intake's park, the worker's answer, and the intake's last step.

## What changed

**A concurrent outbox dispatcher.** Deliveries run on several workers (`sutra.outbox.workers`,
default the lane count, at least 8). One instance's deliveries always go to the same worker, in
order, so per-instance order is what it was; deliveries of different instances run in parallel. A
step that enqueues wakes the dispatcher at once; the tick (`sutra.outbox.tick-interval`) is now the
fallback for retries and for rows another replica enqueued. Delivered rows are deleted in batches.
Retry, backoff, the attempts ceiling, poison handling and incidents are unchanged — the workers run
the same per-delivery code.

**Local deliveries are handed over in-process.** A `local://` delivery is still a durable row,
committed with the sender's step. Once that commit is durable the engine hands the row to its
dispatcher directly instead of claiming it back from the table, and the receiving lane runs it
before new intake. The row becomes claimable only after a 30-second grace, so if the engine dies
first, any engine delivers it after restart; the receiver's inbox dedup absorbs a repeat.

**Fewer durable commits.** Four kinds of bookkeeping no longer wait for their own WAL flush,
because a crash that loses them loses nothing: the inbox dedup row (the step commit that follows
flushes it, and the engine flushes it itself before acknowledging when no step commit follows), the
instance ownership claim (a crashed engine's claim is void anyway), the outbox claim (it only takes
row locks) and the delete of delivered rows (a lost delete means a repeat delivery, which the
outbox has always allowed). The per-channel concurrency gauge is written only for a channel that
declares `max-concurrent-instances`. The server's `synchronous_commit` stays `on`.

**Pools and fairness.** `sutra.datasource.max-connections` (default 8, the old fixed size) sizes
the pool the lanes use; `sutra.datasource.dispatch-max-connections` (default 2) is a separate pool
for the dispatcher and the timer poller, so delivery never waits behind intake for a connection.

**Data-store reads.** A data task reads a value and its revision in one statement. A store can
also opt into a read cache in `datastores.yaml`:

```yaml
datastores:
  - name: refdata
    type: sql
    sql: { url-ref: env:REF_DB_URL, username-ref: env:REF_DB_USER, password-ref: env:REF_DB_PASSWORD }
    cache:
      enabled: true
      maxEntries: 1000
      ttl: PT0S        # the default: revalidate every read by revision
```

With `ttl: PT0S` a cached key costs a revision check instead of a full read, and a write through
any engine — each one bumps the row's revision — applies to the next read. A positive `ttl` serves a
key with no query for that long; writes through this engine still invalidate it at once, but a
write by another replica or by SQL outside the engine shows only after `ttl`. SQL outside the
engine must bump `rev` to be seen by the revision check.

## Measured

Same laptop and disk, PostgreSQL 18 with fsync, synchronous_commit and full_page_writes on:

| | lanes | offered | completed/s | p50 | p99 | WAL flushes per relay |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.6.4 | 1 | 20/s | 13.7 | 44 s | 53 s | 12.1 |
| 0.6.4 | 1 | 100/s | 21.6 | 108 s | 118 s | 12.1 |
| 0.6.5 | 1 (defaults) | 100/s | 70.4 | 6.7 s | 13.2 s | 3.02 |
| 0.6.5 | 8 | 100/s | 99.9 | 19 ms | 46 ms | 2.90 |
| 0.6.5 | 32 | 500/s | 499.0 | 36 ms | 250 ms | 0.57 |

To go past one lane, raise `sutra.engine.shards` and `sutra.datasource.max-connections` together;
the book's *Tuning for throughput* page walks through it, with the commands and their output. The workload is in
`tools/sutra-load-test` (`relay-bench.sh`), so you can measure your own disk.

## Fixes

- **A timer expression that reads an unknown name is refused at load.** A timer body, `q:timeout`
  or `q:retry` expression whose root name nothing provides — not `config`, a declared variable or
  data object, the payload, or a variable the process sets — is now a lint, package and deploy
  error, `SUTRA.CONFIG.BPMN.TIMER_EXPRESSION_UNKNOWN_NAME`, instead of a null when the timer is
  armed. A mistyped duration literal now says which literal was meant: `PT10SEC` → "did you mean
  PT10S?".
- **SQL Server driver.** tiberius 0.13, on rustls 0.23. rustls 0.21 and rustls-webpki 0.101 leave
  the build, and with them six advisories that had been time-boxed. rustls is now compiled with two
  crypto providers, so the engine and the CLI select ring explicitly at start.

## Upgrading

Nothing to do. A deployment that relied on an outbound delivery being sent strictly after the
previous one *of another instance* never had that guarantee and still does not; one instance's
deliveries keep their order. If you embed the engine in your own binary, call
`sutra_engine::serve` (it installs the TLS provider) or `sutra_engine::install_tls_provider()`
before building TLS clients yourself.

## Install

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/startr-trade/sutra:0.6.5
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/startr-trade/sutra/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.6.5
```

The library crates are on crates.io as `sutra-feel = "0.6.5"` and `sutra-dmn = "0.6.5"`.
